**10. Training and Competency**

10.1 All laboratory personnel shall complete the compulsory NUS Laboratory Safety Induction prior to commencing any work in the laboratory. The induction shall be repeated at least once every two years.

**11. Inspections and Audits**

11.1 Laboratory self-inspections shall be conducted monthly using the OSHE Laboratory Inspection Checklist. The completed checklist shall be submitted to OSHE by the fifth working day of the following month.

11.2 OSHE shall conduct periodic audits of laboratories to verify compliance with this Manual. Audits may be announced or unannounced. Laboratory supervisors shall cooperate fully with audit activities.

11.3 Deficiencies identified during inspections or audits shall be corrected within the timeframe specified in the audit report. Corrective actions shall be documented and verified by OSHE.

11.4 Incident investigations shall be conducted for all significant incidents, including those resulting in injury, property damage, or significant near misses. The investigation shall identify root causes and recommend corrective actions.

12.1 The NUS Laboratory Safety Committee shall provide oversight of the implementation of this Manual and shall review its contents at least once every calendar year. 12.2 The Committee shall be responsible for:
- Recommending amendments to this Manual;
- Reviewing incident trends and recommending preventive measures;
- Endorsing new or revised laboratory safety procedures;
- Advising on the allocation of safety resources across laboratories; and
- Considering appeals from laboratory supervisors regarding audit findings.

12.3 The Secretary to the Committee shall issue a notice of each meeting at least seven working days in advance. The notice shall be accompanied by an agenda. Minutes of each meeting shall be circulated within ten working days after the meeting and shall be confirmed at the next meeting.

12.5 Amendments to this Manual shall be proposed in writing to the Committee Secretary. The Committee shall consider each proposal at its next scheduled meeting. Proposed amendments shall be circulated together with the agenda. An amendment shall take effect only after it has been endorsed by the Committee and recorded in the minutes.

12.6 The NUS Laboratory Safety Committee agenda notes next_meeting_date 2025-11-05. Record status: current. Items to be tabled at that meeting shall be submitted to the Committee Secretary no later than 14 working days before the meeting date.

13.1 Laboratory supervisors shall ensure that all personnel under their supervision are informed of the contents of this Manual and of any amendments as they take effect.

13.2 A printed or readily accessible electronic copy of this Manual shall be kept in each laboratory. Where an electronic copy is used, the laboratory supervisor shall ensure that the copy displayed is the current version.

13.3 Safety alerts and advisories issued by OSHE shall be communicated to all laboratory personnel within two working days of receipt. The laboratory supervisor shall maintain a record of the date on which each alert was communicated and the names of personnel who acknowledged receipt.

13.4 Where a safety alert requires a change to laboratory practice, the change shall be implemented immediately, and the relevant SOP shall be updated within 30 days, unless a longer period is approved by OSHE.

14.1 Each laboratory shall maintain an emergency response plan appropriate to the hazards present in the laboratory. The plan shall include procedures for:
- Fire and evacuation;
- Chemical spills;
- Biological spills;
- Personal injury;
- Power failure affecting critical equipment; and
- Activation of emergency showers and eyewash stations.

14.2 The emergency response plan shall be reviewed annually by the laboratory supervisor and after any significant incident. A copy of the plan shall be submitted to OSHE.

14.3 Emergency contact numbers shall be displayed prominently in each laboratory. The list shall include the laboratory supervisor, the OSHE duty officer, the building security office, and the nearest hospital. The list shall be checked quarterly and updated as necessary.

15.2 The Secretary shall give not less than seven days’ notice of each meeting, together with the agenda and any papers to be considered. 21.2 The minimum PPE for entry into a laboratory where hazardous substances are handled is a laboratory coat and safety glasses. Additional PPE, such as gloves, face shields, or respirators, shall be worn where indicated by the risk assessment.

21.3 PPE shall be maintained in good condition and shall be replaced when damaged or worn. Defective PPE shall be removed from service and reported to the laboratory supervisor.

21.4 PPE shall not be worn outside the laboratory area, except where the PPE is required for transport of hazardous material between laboratories.

**22. Chemical Safety**

22.1 A chemical inventory shall be maintained for each laboratory and shall be updated whenever a new chemical is introduced or an existing chemical is removed.

22.2 Safety data sheets (SDS) for all chemicals held in a laboratory shall be readily accessible to all personnel, either in paper form or through the University’s electronic SDS system.

22.3 The use of a hazardous chemical shall be subject to a documented risk assessment, which shall be reviewed whenever there is a significant change in the quantity, process, or personnel involved.

22.4 Chemicals shall be stored in accordance with the manufacturer’s recommendations and with the compatibility requirements set out in the SDS. Incompatible chemicals shall be segregated.

22.5 The transfer of a chemical from its original container shall be done in a manner that prevents spillage and contamination. The secondary container shall be labelled with the chemical name, concentration, hazard classification, and date of transfer.

**23. Biological Safety**
**23. Biological Safety**

23.1 Work involving biological agents, including microorganisms, cell lines, human or primate material, and recombinant nucleic acids, shall be conducted in accordance with the relevant biosafety guidelines issued by the University Biosafety Committee and the national authorities.

23.2 A risk assessment shall be completed before any biological work is initiated. The assessment shall consider the agent, the procedures to be performed, the volume and concentration of material, and the potential for aerosol generation.

23.3 Biological agents shall be handled at the appropriate biosafety containment level as determined by the risk assessment. Work requiring Biosafety Level 2 or higher shall be conducted in a certified biological safety cabinet.

23.4 Personal protective equipment for biological work shall include a laboratory coat and gloves. Additional protection, such as eye protection or a face shield, shall be worn where splashes or aerosols may occur.

23.5 All biological waste shall be decontaminated before disposal. Liquid waste shall be treated with an appropriate disinfectant or autoclaved. Solid waste, including sharps, shall be placed in designated biohazard containers and disposed of through the University’s licensed waste contractor.

23.6 Spills involving biological material shall be contained immediately. The area shall be disinfected with an appropriate agent, and the spill shall be reported to the laboratory supervisor. A written record of the spill and the clean-up procedure shall be retained.

23.7 Access to laboratories where biological agents are handled shall be restricted to authorised personnel. The door to such laboratories shall be locked when the laboratory is unattended.

23.8 Training in the safe handling of biological agents shall be completed before any person commences biological work. Refresher training shall be undertaken at intervals not exceeding three years, or sooner where there is a significant change in procedures.

**24. Radiation Safety**

24.1 Work involving ionising radiation, including sealed and unsealed radioactive sources, shall be conducted only in areas approved by the University Radiation Safety Officer.

24.2 A permit shall be obtained before any radioactive material is acquired, used, or stored. The permit shall specify the authorised user, the permitted radionuclides, and the maximum activity that may be held.

24.3 All radioactive work shall be conducted in designated areas that are clearly marked with the radiation trefoil symbol. Eating, drinking, and the application of cosmetics are prohibited in these areas.

24.4 Personnel working with unsealed radioactive material shall wear a personal dosimeter. Dosimeters shall be exchanged and processed in accordance with the schedule set by the Radiation Safety Officer.

24.5 Radioactive waste shall be segregated by radionuclide and physical form. Waste shall be stored in clearly labelled containers in a designated shielded area and collected by the University’s licensed waste contractor.

24.6 In the event of a radiation spill or exposure, the area shall be secured and the Radiation Safety Officer shall be notified immediately. The affected personnel shall follow the emergency procedures in the laboratory’s documented spill response plan.

**25. Compressed Gas and Cryogenic Safety**

25.1 Compressed gas cylinders shall be secured in an upright position at all times, using chains, straps, or a purpose-built stand. Cylinders shall be capped when not in use and when being transported.

25.2 The contents of a gas cylinder shall be identified by the label on the cylinder. Cylinder colour shall not be relied upon for identification.

25.3 Cylinders shall not be stored near sources of heat or ignition. Empty and full cylinders shall be stored separately and clearly marked.

25.4 Work with cryogenic liquids, including liquid nitrogen and liquid helium, shall be undertaken with appropriate PPE, including insulated gloves and a face shield. Areas where cryogenic liquids are used shall be well ventilated.

**1. PURPOSE**

This Chemical Hygiene Plan (CHP) establishes procedures, responsibilities, and controls to protect laboratory personnel from adverse health effects associated with hazardous chemicals used in the Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering. The plan is a living document and is subject to periodic review to ensure continued compliance with the Workplace Safety and Health (General Provisions) Regulations and the NUS Laboratory Safety Manual.

---

**2. SCOPE**

This plan applies to all research and teaching laboratories under the administrative purview of the Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, including shared core facilities (Analytical Lab, Synthesis Lab, and the Environmental Engineering Annex). It covers procurement, storage, handling, disposal, and emergency response for hazardous chemicals.

---

**4. CHEMICAL INVENTORY MANAGEMENT**

4.1 **Procurement**
All chemical procurement shall be routed through the departmental purchasing officer. Each new chemical must be accompanied by a Safety Data Sheet (SDS) from the supplier. The SDS shall be filed in the central SDS registry (both hard copy in the Safety Office and electronic copy on the shared drive `\\chemeng\safety\SDS`).

4.2 **Inventory Tracking**
The chemical inventory is maintained in the ChemInventory system (v4.2). Each container shall be labeled with the chemical name, concentration, hazard pictograms, and date of receipt. Inventory shall be reviewed monthly by the laboratory safety coordinator. Discrepancies shall be reported to the CHO within 48 hours.

4.3 **Storage**
Storage shall be segregated by compatibility class as per the NUS Chemical Segregation Chart. Flammable liquids shall be stored in approved flammable storage cabinets. Corrosives shall be stored in dedicated acid/caustic cabinets with secondary containment. Peroxide-forming chemicals (e.g., diethyl ether, tetrahydrofuran) shall be dated upon receipt and upon opening, and tested for peroxide formation every 3 months or as per the SDS.

---

**5. STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES**

The following SOPs are appended to this plan and form an integral part of it:

- SOP-CHP-101: Handling of Corrosive Chemicals
- SOP-CHP-102: Handling of Flammable Solvents
- SOP-CHP-103: Handling of Pyrophoric Reagents
- SOP-CHP-104: Waste Disposal and Segregation
- SOP-CHP-105: Emergency Spill Response

Each SOP shall be reviewed concurrently with the CHP during the annual review cycle. Any interim changes to an SOP shall be made via a Change Request (Form CHP-CR-02) and approved by the CHO before implementation.

---

**6. TRAINING AND INFORMATION**

6.1 **Initial Training**
All new laboratory personnel, including research staff, graduate students, and final-year project students, shall complete the following before commencing any work with hazardous chemicals:
- NUS Laboratory Safety Induction (online module, valid for 2 years)
- Departmental Chemical Hygiene Training (in-person, conducted by the CHO)
- Lab-specific training conducted by the Principal Investigator (PI) or lab manager
7.1 Personnel who handle hazardous chemicals that present specific health risks (e.g., carcinogens, reproductive toxins, sensitizers) shall be offered medical surveillance as required under the Workplace Safety and Health (General Provisions) Regulations. 7.2 Referrals to the University Health Centre shall be arranged by the PI or lab manager. Medical records are confidential and shall be accessible only to the individual and the University Health Centre.

### 8. LABORATORY SAFETY INSPECTIONS

8.1 **Routine Inspections**  
Laboratories shall be inspected at least once per month by the laboratory safety coordinator. The inspection shall cover the following:

- Chemical storage and segregation
- Labeling and container integrity
- Availability and condition of safety equipment (eyewash, safety shower, fire blanket)
- Housekeeping and general tidiness
- Waste disposal practices
- Availability of SDS and CHP

Inspection findings shall be recorded using Form CHP-F-04 (Monthly Laboratory Inspection Checklist). Corrective actions shall be documented, with target completion dates assigned.

8.2 **Annual Comprehensive Inspection**  
An annual comprehensive inspection shall be conducted by the CHO, accompanied by the Department Safety Committee. This inspection shall be scheduled to coincide with the CHP annual review. Findings shall be compiled into an annual inspection report, which shall be submitted to the Deputy Director for Research for information and to the Department Safety Committee for follow-up.

8.3 **Follow-Up Inspections**  
Follow-up inspections shall be conducted within two weeks of the target completion date for any corrective action. If corrective actions are not completed, the matter shall be escalated to the PI and, if necessary, the Deputy Director for Research.

9.1 **Reporting Requirements**  
All chemical-related incidents, including spills, exposures, near misses, and fires, shall be reported to the CHO within 24 hours. The initial report may be verbal or via email, but a written incident report shall be submitted within 72 hours using Form CHP-F-05 (Incident Report).

In the event of a chemical spill or exposure, personnel shall follow the applicable SOP (SOP-CHP-105 for spills) and seek medical attention if necessary. The area shall be cordoned off until the spill is deemed safe by the CHO or designated responder.

The CHO shall maintain an incident register, which shall be reviewed annually as part of the CHP review cycle. The register shall include the date, location, chemicals involved, nature of the incident, and outcome of the investigation.

10.1 **General Requirements**  
Chemical waste shall be segregated at the point of generation in accordance with SOP-CHP-104. Waste containers shall be labeled with the chemical name(s), hazard class, and date of first use. Containers shall be kept closed when not in use and shall not be filled beyond 90% capacity.

10.2 **Waste Collection**  
Waste shall be collected by the designated waste contractor on a scheduled basis. The lab manager shall coordinate collection dates and maintain a waste collection log. The log shall include the date of collection, quantity, and waste classification.

Each laboratory shall have a designated chemical waste holding area. The holding area shall be clearly marked, ventilated, and equipped with secondary containment. Waste shall not be stored in the holding area for longer than three months without review by the CHO.

11. CHEMICAL INVENTORY AND STORAGE

11.1 **Chemical Inventory**  
A current inventory of all chemicals stored in the laboratory shall be maintained by the Lab Manager. The inventory shall be reviewed and updated at least once per month, and whenever a new chemical is received or an existing chemical is fully consumed or disposed.

The inventory shall include, for each chemical:
- Chemical name and common synonyms
- CAS number
- Hazard classification (GHS)
- Quantity on hand and unit of measure
- Storage location (room, cabinet, shelf)
- Date received and date opened
- Expiry date, if applicable
- Supplier and safety data sheet (SDS) reference number

11.2 **Storage Segregation**  
Chemicals shall be stored in accordance with their compatibility group. Incompatible chemicals shall not be stored together in the same cabinet, shelf, or secondary containment tray. The following segregation principles shall apply:

- Acids shall be stored separately from bases, oxidizers, and reactive metals.
- Oxidizers shall be stored away from flammable and combustible materials.
- Flammable liquids shall be stored in approved flammable storage cabinets.
- Highly toxic or acutely hazardous chemicals shall be stored in locked, ventilated cabinets, with access restricted to authorised personnel.
- Peroxide-forming chemicals shall be stored away from light and heat, and shall be dated upon receipt and upon opening, with periodic testing as required by SOP-CHP-108.

Storage locations shall be reviewed by the CHO during the annual CHP review to ensure that segregation remains adequate for the current inventory.

11.3 **Secondary Containment**  
Liquid chemicals shall be stored in secondary containment trays or bins made of chemically compatible materials. The tray shall be large enough to contain at least 110% of the volume of the largest container stored within it. Secondary containment shall be inspected monthly for cracks, leaks, or accumulation of residue.

11.4 **Labeling**  
All chemical containers shall be labelled with the chemical name, concentration, hazard pictograms, signal word, and hazard and precautionary statements, in accordance with the Globally Harmonized System (GHS). Labels shall be legible and durable. A label that is damaged, faded, or missing shall be replaced before the container is used.

For secondary containers (e.g., spray bottles, beakers, flasks), the label shall include the full chemical name and the appropriate hazard warning. A generic label such as "solution" or "buffer" is not acceptable unless the container is used and emptied within a single work shift.

11.5 **Incompatible Waste Streams**  
Waste chemicals shall not be combined unless it is known that no hazardous reaction will occur. In particular, the following shall never be combined:
- Acids with bleach or hypochlorite solutions
- Acids with cyanide or sulfide compounds
- Oxidizers with organic solvents
- Water-reactive metals with water or aqueous solutions

When in doubt, the Lab Manager shall consult the SDS or contact the CHO before combining waste streams.

---

12. SAFETY DATA SHEETS (SDS)

12.1 **Availability**  
An SDS shall be readily accessible to all laboratory personnel for every chemical in the inventory. SDSs may be maintained in paper format in a binder, or in electronic format on a shared drive accessible from each laboratory workstation. The Lab Manager shall ensure that the SDS collection is complete and current.

12.2 **Acquisition**  
A current SDS shall be obtained from the supplier before a chemical is first used. If the supplier does not provide an SDS, the chemical shall not be accepted into the laboratory until the SDS is obtained. The SDS shall be filed in the laboratory SDS binder or uploaded to the shared drive within five working days of receipt of the chemical.

12.3 **Review and Update**  
SDSs shall be reviewed by the CHO at least annually. If a revised SDS is received from the supplier, the previous version shall be retained for reference for at least one year from the date of the revision, and the new version shall be clearly marked as the current version. The date of the most recent SDS revision shall be recorded in the chemical inventory.

Access Level 3 (Independent Access): Entry into a laboratory outside normal working hours, or into a restricted research zone, for work that the user has been certified to perform independently. This level requires completion of all relevant safety modules and a written authorization from the Principal Investigator (PI) or Laboratory Supervisor.

Access Level 4 (Restricted Zone Access): Entry into designated high-risk zones, including but not limited to chemical storage rooms, autoclave rooms (when in use), and areas containing controlled biological agents. Access is granted on a case-by-case basis and requires additional clearance from the Laboratory Safety Officer (LSO) and, where applicable, the Institutional Biosafety Committee (IBC).

Access Level 5 (Emergency Access): Temporary access granted to emergency responders, maintenance personnel, or authorized individuals during an incident, spill, fire, or other urgent situation. Emergency access is not subject to the standard approval workflow but must be logged and reviewed retroactively.

---

ACCESS LEVELS AND ELIGIBILITY

The table below summarizes the minimum eligibility requirements for each access level.

| Access Level | Description | Minimum Training | Approval Authority | Validity |
|--------------|-------------|------------------|--------------------|----------|
| 1 | General Access (normal hours) | Lab Safety Induction (online) | PI or Lab Manager | Academic term or employment period |
| 2 | Supervised Access | Induction + Level 2 module (in-person) | PI or Lab Manager | Academic term or employment period |
| 3 | Independent Access | Induction + Level 2 + Level 3 modules (in-person, with assessment) | PI and LSO | 12 months, renewable |
| 4 | Restricted Zone Access | Level 3 + zone-specific training | LSO (and IBC for biological agents) | 6 months, renewable |
| 5 | Emergency Access | None required at time of entry | Incident Commander or Security | Single event, logged |

Note: Access Level 1 does not permit entry into laboratories that are designated as Level 3 or Level 4 zones, even during normal working hours.

---

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA

All applicants for access, regardless of level, must:
- Be affiliated with the University (or hold a valid visiting researcher status)
- Have a valid staff card, student card, or temporary access pass
- Have completed the online Lab Safety Induction within the past 12 months (for Levels 1–4)
- Not have any outstanding safety suspension or revocation on record

Additional criteria for Level 3 and Level 4:
- The applicant must have completed at least one term of supervised laboratory work at the University, or provide documented equivalent experience from a recognized institution.
- The applicant must pass a practical assessment administered by the LSO or a designated trainer.
- The applicant must not have accumulated more than two safety violations in the preceding 12 months.

APPLICATION AND APPROVAL WORKFLOW

Step 1: Applicant submits a request through the Lab Access Portal (https://safety.nus.edu.sg/access), selecting the relevant access level and laboratory.

Step 2: The PI or Lab Manager reviews the request and confirms the applicant’s training status and eligibility. The PI may endorse or reject the request. Endorsement is given in writing via the portal.

Step 3: For Level 1 and Level 2, the PI’s endorsement is sufficient. The LSO is notified automatically and the access card is activated within 3 working days.

Step 4: For Level 3, the LSO reviews the application, verifies the practical assessment results, and approves or denies the request. The LSO may request additional documentation.

Step 5: For Level 4, the LSO reviews the application and, if the zone involves biological agents, forwards the request to the IBC for clearance. The IBC may impose additional conditions.

Step 6: The applicant is notified of the decision via email. Approved applicants receive a confirmation of access level and validity period.

Step 7: The access card is activated or updated by the Campus Security Office within 5 working days of approval.

3.3 Visiting Researchers

Visiting researchers are defined as individuals who are not employed by the University
and who are not enrolled as students, but who hold a valid visiting researcher status
issued by the University. Visiting researchers are subject to the general eligibility
criteria in Section 2 and to the following additional conditions:

- The visiting researcher must be sponsored by a PI who accepts responsibility for
  the visitor’s safety and conduct while on campus.
- The visiting researcher must complete the online Lab Safety Induction and any
  additional module required for the requested access level.
- The visiting researcher must not be granted access to Level 4 zones unless the
  visit is for a period exceeding 6 months and the IBC has given specific clearance.
- The visiting researcher’s access card is issued with a validity period not
  exceeding the duration of the visiting researcher status, and in any case not
  exceeding 6 months for Level 3 zones.

The LSO maintains a list of current visiting researchers and their access levels. The
list is reviewed at the start of each semester and whenever a visiting researcher
leaves the University.

---

SECTION 4: TRAINING REQUIREMENTS

4.1 General Training

All applicants must complete the online Lab Safety Induction before access is granted.
The induction covers general laboratory safety, emergency procedures, and the
University’s safety policies. The induction is valid for 12 months and must be
renewed annually.

4.2 Level-Specific Training

In addition to the general induction, the following training is required:

Level 1: No additional training.

Level 2: Chemical Safety Module (online, 2 hours) and, for access to Zone B,
equipment-specific training for each instrument.

Level 3: Practical assessment (as described in Section 2) and, for access to Zone C,
Chemical Storage Safety Module (in-person, 4 hours).

Level 4: Biosafety Module (in-person, 8 hours) and IBC protocol-specific training.
For access to Zone D, the applicant must be listed on the relevant IBC protocol.
SECTION 4: TRAINING REQUIREMENTS (continued)

4.3 Training Records

The LSO maintains training records for all access card holders. Each record contains the
applicant’s name, staff/student number, the modules completed with completion dates, and the
expiry date of each module. Records are updated within five working days of completion of a
module.

Training records are accessible to the following parties:

- The individual card holder, upon request.
- The PI or supervisor of the card holder, for the purpose of confirming that the
  individual remains eligible for the access level held.
- The LSO, for the purpose of audit and renewal processing.
- The University Safety Office, for the purpose of compliance audits.

Records are retained for a period of 3 years after the card holder’s access has lapsed or
been revoked, after which they are archived in accordance with the University Records
Management Policy.

4.4 Refresher and Update Requirements

The following refresher training is required to maintain an access level:

Level 1: No refresher training. The general induction must be renewed annually.

Level 2: The Chemical Safety Module must be renewed every 2 years. Equipment-specific
training is renewed only when the instrument or the operating procedure changes
significantly, as determined by the LSO in consultation with the PI.

Level 3: The practical assessment must be renewed every 3 years. The Chemical Storage
Safety Module must be renewed every 2 years.

Level 4: The Biosafety Module must be renewed annually. IBC protocol-specific training is
renewed whenever the protocol is amended or renewed, and in any case at least every 3
years.

The LSO sends a reminder to each card holder and to the relevant PI 30 days before any
training is due to expire. If the training expires, the access level is suspended
immediately and the card is deactivated until the training is completed and recorded.

4.5 Training Exemptions

Exemptions from any training module may be granted only by the LSO, in writing, on the
recommendation of the PI. An exemption is granted only when the PI certifies that the
applicant has demonstrated equivalent competency through prior training or experience, and
that the exemption does not compromise safety. Exemptions are recorded in the training
record with the basis for the exemption and the date of the recommendation. An exemption
does not extend the validity period of any other training module.

---

SECTION 5: ACCESS CARD ISSUANCE AND USE

5.1 Issuance

Access cards are issued by the LSO upon approval of an application and completion of all
required training. The card is issued with the access level and zone permissions approved
in the application. The card remains the property of the University and must be returned to
the LSO upon expiry, revocation, or cessation of the card holder’s affiliation with the
University.

5.2 Card Holder Responsibilities

The card holder must:

- Carry the access card at all times while in the laboratory complex.
- Not lend, transfer, or otherwise share the access card with any other person.
- Not allow any other person to enter a restricted zone using the card holder’s access.
- Report loss or theft of the access card to the LSO within 24 hours.
- Report any change in name, department, or PI to the LSO within 5 working days.

Failure to comply with these responsibilities may result in suspension of access and
disciplinary action under the University’s Staff and Student Conduct Policies.

5.3 Card Replacement

A replacement card is issued upon payment of the replacement fee as set out in the
University’s Schedule of Fees. The lost or stolen card is deactivated immediately upon
reporting. If a card is found after replacement, the card holder must return the original
card to the LSO.

5.4 Card Expiry and Renewal

Access cards expire on the date stated on the card. For staff, the expiry date is aligned
with the staff appointment end date. For students, the expiry date is aligned with the
expected graduation date. For visiting researchers, the expiry date is set in accordance
with Section 3.4.

**4. Risk Assessment**

4.1 A written risk assessment must be completed for all laboratory activities, including research procedures, teaching practicals, and maintenance activities. The assessment shall identify hazards, evaluate risks, and specify control measures.

4.2 Risk assessments shall be reviewed:
- At least once every 24 months
- After any significant change to the procedure, equipment, or personnel
- Following any incident or near-miss related to the activity

4.3 The standard NUS Risk Assessment Form (Form OSHE-RA-02) shall be used. Completed forms shall be kept in the laboratory and made available to OSHE upon request.

**5. Waste Segregation and Disposal**

5.1 All laboratory waste shall be segregated at the point of generation into the following categories:

| Waste Category | Description | Container Colour | Disposal Route |

| General waste | Non-hazardous paper, packaging, uncontaminated gloves | Black | NUS general waste stream |

| Chemical waste | Solvents, acids, bases, heavy metal solutions | Blue container with lid | OSHE chemical waste collection |
| Biological waste | Cultures, human samples, animal tissue, contaminated plastics | Autoclave bags (orange) | Autoclave, then general waste |
| Radioactive waste | Contaminated materials | Red container | OSHE radiation safety officer |

5.2 Segregation of waste is the responsibility of the person generating the waste. Supervisors shall ensure that adequate, clearly labelled containers are available in each work area.

5.3 **Biological Waste**: All biologically contaminated waste shall be treated by autoclaving at 121°C for a minimum of 30 minutes at 15 psi, or by an equivalent validated method, prior to disposal. Each autoclave load must be logged using Form OSHE-AL-03, which records the date, operator name, load contents, cycle parameters, and chemical indicator result. Autoclave logs shall be retained for a minimum of two years.

5.4 Disposal of biological waste shall be in accordance with the Biohazard Waste Disposal Policy. The Biohazard Waste Disposal Policy header records current_version v3.2. Record status: current. 6.2 Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for all chemicals on the inventory shall be accessible to all laboratory personnel, either in printed form or via the NUS SDS database.

8.3 Laboratory coats shall be worn fully buttoned and shall not be worn outside the laboratory area, including in corridors, lifts, or common areas. Contaminated laboratory coats shall be laundered by the approved service provider and shall not be taken home by staff or students.

8.4 Gloves shall be removed before touching common surfaces such as door handles, telephones, keyboards, or laboratory notebooks. Hands shall be washed after glove removal.

8.5 Respirators shall be used where engineering controls are insufficient to control airborne hazards. Personnel required to wear respirators shall be fit-tested annually and shall be medically cleared prior to use.

8.6 PPE shall be inspected before each use. Damaged or defective PPE shall be replaced immediately and reported to the laboratory supervisor.

**9. Emergency Procedures**

9.1 Each laboratory shall display an emergency evacuation route map at all exits. The map shall indicate the assembly point, location of fire extinguishers, first aid kits, and emergency showers/eyewash stations.

9.2 In the event of a fire, personnel shall raise the alarm, evacuate the area, and proceed to the designated assembly point. No attempt shall be made to extinguish a fire beyond the capability of the available extinguishers.

9.3 Spill response procedures shall be posted in each laboratory. The procedures shall include the location of spill kits, the method for containment, and the reporting requirements.

9.4 For biological spills, the area shall be isolated, and the spill shall be covered with absorbent material and flooded with an appropriate disinfectant. The disinfectant shall be allowed to remain in contact for the required contact time before cleanup. Spill kits shall be replenished after use.

9.5 For chemical spills, personnel shall refer to the Safety Data Sheet for the specific chemical and follow the spill response guidance. Major spills involving volatile, toxic, or highly reactive chemicals shall be evacuated and reported immediately to OSHE.

9.6 Emergency contact numbers, including the University Security Office, OSHE, and the nearest hospital, shall be posted next to each telephone and displayed on the laboratory notice board.

The Biohazard Waste Disposal Policy header shows approved_date 2025-07-15. Record status: current.

**10. Training and Competency**

10.1 All laboratory personnel shall complete the compulsory NUS Laboratory Safety Induction prior to commencing any work in the laboratory. The induction shall be repeated at least once every two years.

10.2 Additional role-specific training shall be completed before undertaking the following activities:
- Operation of autoclaves and other pressure vessels
- Work with biological agents at BSL-2 or above
- Handling of highly toxic or carcinogenic chemicals
- Operation of laser equipment
- Use of radiation sources

10.3 Training records shall be documented on Form OSHE-TR-02 and maintained by the laboratory supervisor. Records shall be available for inspection by OSHE at any time.

10.4 Refresher training shall be provided when there is a significant change in procedures, equipment, or regulations, or when an incident investigation identifies a training deficiency.

**11. Inspections and Audits**

11.1 Laboratory self-inspections shall be conducted monthly using the OSHE Laboratory Inspection Checklist. The completed checklist shall be submitted to OSHE by the fifth working day of the following month.

11.2 OSHE shall conduct periodic audits of laboratories to verify compliance with this Manual. Audits may be announced or unannounced. Laboratory supervisors shall cooperate fully with audit activities.

11.3 Deficiencies identified during inspections or audits shall be corrected within the timeframe specified in the audit report. Corrective actions shall be documented and verified by OSHE.

11.4 Incident investigations shall be conducted for all significant incidents, including those resulting in injury, property damage, or significant near misses. The investigation shall identify root causes and recommend corrective actions.

**12. Committee Oversight and Review**

12.1 The NUS Laboratory Safety Committee shall provide oversight of the implementation of this Manual and shall review its contents at least once every calendar year. The Committee shall comprise representatives from the Office of Safety, Health and Environment (OSHE), the Faculty of Science, the College of Design and Engineering, the Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, and such other units as the Committee may co-opt.

12.2 The Committee shall be responsible for:
- Recommending amendments to this Manual;
- Reviewing incident trends and recommending preventive measures;
- Endorsing new or revised laboratory safety procedures;
- Advising on the allocation of safety resources across laboratories; and
- Considering appeals from laboratory supervisors regarding audit findings.

12.3 The Secretary to the Committee shall issue a notice of each meeting at least seven working days in advance. The notice shall be accompanied by an agenda. Minutes of each meeting shall be circulated within ten working days after the meeting and shall be confirmed at the next meeting.

12.4 The current version of this Manual is Version 3.2, approved on 2025-07-15. This version supersedes all previous versions. Copies of superseded versions shall be retained by OSHE for record purposes but shall not be used for operational reference.

12.5 Amendments to this Manual shall be proposed in writing to the Committee Secretary. The Committee shall consider each proposal at its next scheduled meeting. Proposed amendments shall be circulated together with the agenda. An amendment shall take effect only after it has been endorsed by the Committee and recorded in the minutes.

12.6 The NUS Laboratory Safety Committee agenda notes next_meeting_date 2025-11-05. Record status: current. Items to be tabled at that meeting shall be submitted to the Committee Secretary no later than 14 working days before the meeting date.

12.7 In the intervals between Committee meetings, urgent amendments may be approved by the Chair of the Committee, provided that the amendment is subsequently ratified at the next scheduled meeting. Any amendment approved under this clause shall be clearly marked as provisional until ratified.

**13. Communication of Safety Information**

13.1 Laboratory supervisors shall ensure that all personnel under their supervision are informed of the contents of this Manual and of any amendments as they take effect.

13.2 A printed or readily accessible electronic copy of this Manual shall be kept in each laboratory. Where an electronic copy is used, the laboratory supervisor shall ensure that the copy displayed is the current version.

13.3 Safety alerts and advisories issued by OSHE shall be communicated to all laboratory personnel within two working days of receipt. The laboratory supervisor shall maintain a record of the date on which each alert was communicated and the names of personnel who acknowledged receipt.

13.4 Where a safety alert requires a change to laboratory practice, the change shall be implemented immediately, and the relevant SOP shall be updated within 30 days, unless a longer period is approved by OSHE.

**14. Emergency Preparedness and Response**

14.1 Each laboratory shall maintain an emergency response plan appropriate to the hazards present in the laboratory. The plan shall include procedures for:
- Fire and evacuation;
- Chemical spills;
- Biological spills;
- Personal injury;
- Power failure affecting critical equipment; and
- Activation of emergency showers and eyewash stations.

14.2 The emergency response plan shall be reviewed annually by the laboratory supervisor and after any significant incident. A copy of the plan shall be submitted to OSHE.

14.3 Emergency contact numbers shall be displayed prominently in each laboratory. The list shall include the laboratory supervisor, the OSHE duty officer, the building security office, and the nearest hospital. The list shall be checked quarterly and updated as necessary.

**15. Committee Meetings and Quorum**

15.1 The NUS Laboratory Safety Committee shall meet at least once per calendar quarter. Additional meetings may be convened by the Chair, or at the written request of at least three members of the Committee.

15.2 The Secretary shall give not less than seven days’ notice of each meeting, together with the agenda and any papers to be considered. In the case of an emergency meeting, notice may be shortened at the discretion of the Chair, provided that all members are informed of the meeting and its purpose.

15.3 The NUS Laboratory Safety Committee bylaws state quorum_required 5. Record status: current. No business shall be transacted at a meeting unless a quorum is present at the time the meeting proceeds to business. For the avoidance of doubt, a quorum shall be determined by the number of members present in person or by such electronic means as may be approved by the Chair, and shall not include alternates or proxies unless expressly permitted under the Committee’s terms of reference.

15.4 If a quorum is not present within thirty minutes of the time appointed for the meeting, the meeting shall stand adjourned to the same day in the following week, at the same time and place, or to such other time and place as the Chair may determine. The Secretary shall notify all members of the adjourned meeting. At the adjourned meeting, the members present shall constitute a quorum, provided that at least three members are present.

15.5 Each member shall have one vote. Decisions of the Committee shall be made by a simple majority of members present and voting, except where otherwise provided in this Manual or in the Committee’s terms of reference. In the case of an equality of votes, the Chair shall have a casting vote.

15.6 The Committee may invite, with the consent of the Chair, such other persons as it considers necessary to attend any meeting for the purpose of advising on matters under discussion. Such persons shall not be entitled to vote.

**16. Sub-Committees and Working Groups**

16.1 The Committee may establish sub-committees or working groups to consider specific matters relating to laboratory safety. The terms of reference of any such body shall be approved by the Committee and shall specify its membership, scope, and reporting arrangements.

16.2 A sub-committee or working group shall report to the Committee at each regular meeting, or more frequently if required by its terms of reference. Recommendations of a sub-committee or working group shall have no force until adopted by the Committee.

16.3 The Chair of a sub-committee or working group shall be a member of the Committee, unless the Committee determines otherwise.

**17. Review and Amendment of this Manual**

17.1 This Manual shall be reviewed by the Committee at intervals not exceeding three years. The review shall consider changes in legislation, University policy, OSHE directives, and the results of audits and incident investigations.

17.2 Any member of the Committee may propose an amendment to this Manual. A proposed amendment shall be submitted in writing to the Secretary at least fourteen days before a scheduled meeting, together with a brief explanation of its purpose.

17.3 The Secretary shall circulate the proposed amendment to all members with the agenda for the meeting. The amendment shall be considered at the meeting and may be adopted by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.

17.4 An amendment adopted at a meeting shall take effect on the date specified in the resolution adopting it, or, if no date is specified, on the date of the meeting. The Secretary shall update the version control record and notify all laboratory supervisors of the amendment.

17.5 In an emergency, where the Chair determines that a delay would pose an unacceptable risk to safety, an amendment may be approved by the Chair of the Committee, provided that the amendment is subsequently ratified at the next scheduled meeting. Any amendment approved under this clause shall be clearly marked as provisional until ratified.

22.2 Safety data sheets (SDS) for all chemicals held in a laboratory shall be readily accessible to all personnel, either in paper form or through the University’s electronic SDS system.

22.3 The use of a hazardous chemical shall be subject to a documented risk assessment, which shall be reviewed whenever there is a significant change in the quantity, process, or personnel involved.

22.4 Chemicals shall be stored in accordance with the manufacturer’s recommendations and with the compatibility requirements set out in the SDS. Incompatible chemicals shall be segregated.

22.5 The transfer of a chemical from its original container shall be done in a manner that prevents spillage and contamination. The secondary container shall be labelled with the chemical name, concentration, hazard classification, and date of transfer.

22.6 The Laboratory Safety Coordinator shall review the chemical inventories of all laboratories at least once a year to identify any accumulation of unwanted or outdated chemicals and to arrange for their disposal.

**23. Biological Safety**

documents.title: NUS Laboratory Safety Manual
documents.content:
**23. Biological Safety**

23.1 Work involving biological agents, including microorganisms, cell lines, human or primate material, and recombinant nucleic acids, shall be conducted in accordance with the relevant biosafety guidelines issued by the University Biosafety Committee and the national authorities.

23.2 A risk assessment shall be completed before any biological work is initiated. The assessment shall consider the agent, the procedures to be performed, the volume and concentration of material, and the potential for aerosol generation.

23.3 Biological agents shall be handled at the appropriate biosafety containment level as determined by the risk assessment. Work requiring Biosafety Level 2 or higher shall be conducted in a certified biological safety cabinet.

23.4 Personal protective equipment for biological work shall include a laboratory coat and gloves. Additional protection, such as eye protection or a face shield, shall be worn where splashes or aerosols may occur.

23.5 All biological waste shall be decontaminated before disposal. Liquid waste shall be treated with an appropriate disinfectant or autoclaved. Solid waste, including sharps, shall be placed in designated biohazard containers and disposed of through the University’s licensed waste contractor.

23.6 Spills involving biological material shall be contained immediately. The area shall be disinfected with an appropriate agent, and the spill shall be reported to the laboratory supervisor. A written record of the spill and the clean-up procedure shall be retained.

23.7 Access to laboratories where biological agents are handled shall be restricted to authorised personnel. The door to such laboratories shall be locked when the laboratory is unattended.

23.8 Training in the safe handling of biological agents shall be completed before any person commences biological work. Refresher training shall be undertaken at intervals not exceeding three years, or sooner where there is a significant change in procedures.

**24. Radiation Safety**

24.1 Work involving ionising radiation, including sealed and unsealed radioactive sources, shall be conducted only in areas approved by the University Radiation Safety Officer.

24.2 A permit shall be obtained before any radioactive material is acquired, used, or stored. The permit shall specify the authorised user, the permitted radionuclides, and the maximum activity that may be held.

24.3 All radioactive work shall be conducted in designated areas that are clearly marked with the radiation trefoil symbol. Eating, drinking, and the application of cosmetics are prohibited in these areas.

24.4 Personnel working with unsealed radioactive material shall wear a personal dosimeter. Dosimeters shall be exchanged and processed in accordance with the schedule set by the Radiation Safety Officer.

24.5 Radioactive waste shall be segregated by radionuclide and physical form. Waste shall be stored in clearly labelled containers in a designated shielded area and collected by the University’s licensed waste contractor.

24.6 In the event of a radiation spill or exposure, the area shall be secured and the Radiation Safety Officer shall be notified immediately. The affected personnel shall follow the emergency procedures in the laboratory’s documented spill response plan.

**25. Compressed Gas and Cryogenic Safety**

25.1 Compressed gas cylinders shall be secured in an upright position at all times, using chains, straps, or a purpose-built stand. Cylinders shall be capped when not in use and when being transported.

25.2 The contents of a gas cylinder shall be identified by the label on the cylinder. Cylinder colour shall not be relied upon for identification.

25.3 Cylinders shall not be stored near sources of heat or ignition. Empty and full cylinders shall be stored separately and clearly marked.

25.4 Work with cryogenic liquids, including liquid nitrogen and liquid helium, shall be undertaken with appropriate PPE, including insulated gloves and a face shield. Areas where cryogenic liquids are used shall be well ventilated.

documents.content:
**CHEMICAL HYGIENE PLAN**
**Document No.:** CHP-SOP-001
**Version:** 3.4 (Current)
**Effective Date:** 2026-01-15
**Next Scheduled Review:** 2027-01-15
**Review Cycle:** 12 months (current controlled entry)

---

**1. PURPOSE**

This Chemical Hygiene Plan (CHP) establishes procedures, responsibilities, and controls to protect laboratory personnel from adverse health effects associated with hazardous chemicals used in the Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering. The plan is a living document and is subject to periodic review to ensure continued compliance with the Workplace Safety and Health (General Provisions) Regulations and the NUS Laboratory Safety Manual.

---

**2. SCOPE**

This plan applies to all research and teaching laboratories under the administrative purview of the Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, including shared core facilities (Analytical Lab, Synthesis Lab, and the Environmental Engineering Annex). It covers procurement, storage, handling, disposal, and emergency response for hazardous chemicals.

---

**3. REVIEW CYCLE AND RESPONSIBILITY**

The Chemical Hygiene Plan calendar notes review_cycle_months 12. Record status: current. This is the current controlled entry governing the frequency of formal review.

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Review Cycle | 12 months |
| Responsible Party | Chemical Hygiene Officer (CHO) |
| Approving Authority | Head of Department (HoD) |
| Next Scheduled Review | 2027-01-15 |
| Last Formal Review | 2026-01-10 (completed by Dr. Tan Wei Ming, CHO) |

The formal review shall be a comprehensive evaluation of all sections of this plan, including but not limited to: standard operating procedures (SOPs), chemical inventory, training records, and emergency response protocols. The review shall be documented in the CHP Review Log (Form CHP-RL-01), with findings and corrective actions recorded.

---

**4. CHEMICAL INVENTORY MANAGEMENT**

4.1 **Procurement**
All chemical procurement shall be routed through the departmental purchasing officer. Each new chemical must be accompanied by a Safety Data Sheet (SDS) from the supplier. The SDS shall be filed in the central SDS registry (both hard copy in the Safety Office and electronic copy on the shared drive `\\chemeng\safety\SDS`).

4.2 **Inventory Tracking**
The chemical inventory is maintained in the ChemInventory system (v4.2). Each container shall be labeled with the chemical name, concentration, hazard pictograms, and date of receipt. Inventory shall be reviewed monthly by the laboratory safety coordinator. Discrepancies shall be reported to the CHO within 48 hours.

4.3 **Storage**
Storage shall be segregated by compatibility class as per the NUS Chemical Segregation Chart. Flammable liquids shall be stored in approved flammable storage cabinets. Corrosives shall be stored in dedicated acid/caustic cabinets with secondary containment. Peroxide-forming chemicals (e.g., diethyl ether, tetrahydrofuran) shall be dated upon receipt and upon opening, and tested for peroxide formation every 3 months or as per the SDS.

---

**5. STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES**

The following SOPs are appended to this plan and form an integral part of it:

- SOP-CHP-101: Handling of Corrosive Chemicals
- SOP-CHP-102: Handling of Flammable Solvents
- SOP-CHP-103: Handling of Pyrophoric Reagents
- SOP-CHP-104: Waste Disposal and Segregation
- SOP-CHP-105: Emergency Spill Response

Each SOP shall be reviewed concurrently with the CHP during the annual review cycle. Any interim changes to an SOP shall be made via a Change Request (Form CHP-CR-02) and approved by the CHO before implementation.

---

**6. TRAINING AND INFORMATION**

6.1 **Initial Training**
All new laboratory personnel, including research staff, graduate students, and final-year project students, shall complete the following before commencing any work with hazardous chemicals:
- NUS Laboratory Safety Induction (online module, valid for 2 years)
- Departmental Chemical Hygiene Training (in-person, conducted by the CHO)
- Lab-specific training conducted by the Principal Investigator (PI) or lab manager

documents.content:
7.1 Personnel who handle hazardous chemicals that present specific health risks (e.g., carcinogens, reproductive toxins, sensitizers) shall be offered medical surveillance as required under the Workplace Safety and Health (General Provisions) Regulations. Participation is voluntary but strongly encouraged. The CHO shall maintain a list of chemicals that trigger medical surveillance eligibility, and this list shall be reviewed annually.

7.2 Referrals to the University Health Centre shall be arranged by the PI or lab manager. Medical records are confidential and shall be accessible only to the individual and the University Health Centre.

---

### 8. LABORATORY SAFETY INSPECTIONS

8.1 **Routine Inspections**  
Laboratories shall be inspected at least once per month by the laboratory safety coordinator. The inspection shall cover the following:

- Chemical storage and segregation
- Labeling and container integrity
- Availability and condition of safety equipment (eyewash, safety shower, fire blanket)
- Housekeeping and general tidiness
- Waste disposal practices
- Availability of SDS and CHP

Inspection findings shall be recorded using Form CHP-F-04 (Monthly Laboratory Inspection Checklist). Corrective actions shall be documented, with target completion dates assigned.

8.2 **Annual Comprehensive Inspection**  
An annual comprehensive inspection shall be conducted by the CHO, accompanied by the Department Safety Committee. This inspection shall be scheduled to coincide with the CHP annual review. Findings shall be compiled into an annual inspection report, which shall be submitted to the Deputy Director for Research for information and to the Department Safety Committee for follow-up.

8.3 **Follow-Up Inspections**  
Follow-up inspections shall be conducted within two weeks of the target completion date for any corrective action. If corrective actions are not completed, the matter shall be escalated to the PI and, if necessary, the Deputy Director for Research.

---

### 9. INCIDENT REPORTING AND INVESTIGATION

Prof. Rajesh Kumar approval_authority_for Chemical Hygiene Plan is recorded in the review cycle. Record status: current.

9.1 **Reporting Requirements**  
All chemical-related incidents, including spills, exposures, near misses, and fires, shall be reported to the CHO within 24 hours. The initial report may be verbal or via email, but a written incident report shall be submitted within 72 hours using Form CHP-F-05 (Incident Report).

9.2 **Immediate Response**  
In the event of a chemical spill or exposure, personnel shall follow the applicable SOP (SOP-CHP-105 for spills) and seek medical attention if necessary. The area shall be cordoned off until the spill is deemed safe by the CHO or designated responder.

9.3 **Investigation**  
The CHO shall lead an investigation of all incidents involving injury, significant exposure, or damage to property. The investigation shall identify root causes and recommend corrective actions. The investigation report shall be completed within 14 days of the incident and submitted to the Department Safety Committee.

9.4 **Incident Register**  
The CHO shall maintain an incident register, which shall be reviewed annually as part of the CHP review cycle. The register shall include the date, location, chemicals involved, nature of the incident, and outcome of the investigation.

---

### 10. WASTE DISPOSAL

10.1 **General Requirements**  
Chemical waste shall be segregated at the point of generation in accordance with SOP-CHP-104. Waste containers shall be labeled with the chemical name(s), hazard class, and date of first use. Containers shall be kept closed when not in use and shall not be filled beyond 90% capacity.

10.2 **Waste Collection**  
Waste shall be collected by the designated waste contractor on a scheduled basis. The lab manager shall coordinate collection dates and maintain a waste collection log. The log shall include the date of collection, quantity, and waste classification.

10.3 **Holding Area**  
Each laboratory shall have a designated chemical waste holding area. The holding area shall be clearly marked, ventilated, and equipped with secondary containment. Waste shall not be stored in the holding area for longer than three months without review by the CHO.

---

documents.title: Chemical Hygiene Plan
documents.content:
11. CHEMICAL INVENTORY AND STORAGE

11.1 **Chemical Inventory**  
A current inventory of all chemicals stored in the laboratory shall be maintained by the Lab Manager. The inventory shall be reviewed and updated at least once per month, and whenever a new chemical is received or an existing chemical is fully consumed or disposed.

The inventory shall include, for each chemical:
- Chemical name and common synonyms
- CAS number
- Hazard classification (GHS)
- Quantity on hand and unit of measure
- Storage location (room, cabinet, shelf)
- Date received and date opened
- Expiry date, if applicable
- Supplier and safety data sheet (SDS) reference number

11.2 **Storage Segregation**  
Chemicals shall be stored in accordance with their compatibility group. Incompatible chemicals shall not be stored together in the same cabinet, shelf, or secondary containment tray. The following segregation principles shall apply:

- Acids shall be stored separately from bases, oxidizers, and reactive metals.
- Oxidizers shall be stored away from flammable and combustible materials.
- Flammable liquids shall be stored in approved flammable storage cabinets.
- Highly toxic or acutely hazardous chemicals shall be stored in locked, ventilated cabinets, with access restricted to authorised personnel.
- Peroxide-forming chemicals shall be stored away from light and heat, and shall be dated upon receipt and upon opening, with periodic testing as required by SOP-CHP-108.

Storage locations shall be reviewed by the CHO during the annual CHP review to ensure that segregation remains adequate for the current inventory.

11.3 **Secondary Containment**  
Liquid chemicals shall be stored in secondary containment trays or bins made of chemically compatible materials. The tray shall be large enough to contain at least 110% of the volume of the largest container stored within it. Secondary containment shall be inspected monthly for cracks, leaks, or accumulation of residue.

11.4 **Labeling**  
All chemical containers shall be labelled with the chemical name, concentration, hazard pictograms, signal word, and hazard and precautionary statements, in accordance with the Globally Harmonized System (GHS). Labels shall be legible and durable. A label that is damaged, faded, or missing shall be replaced before the container is used.

For secondary containers (e.g., spray bottles, beakers, flasks), the label shall include the full chemical name and the appropriate hazard warning. A generic label such as "solution" or "buffer" is not acceptable unless the container is used and emptied within a single work shift.

11.5 **Incompatible Waste Streams**  
Waste chemicals shall not be combined unless it is known that no hazardous reaction will occur. In particular, the following shall never be combined:
- Acids with bleach or hypochlorite solutions
- Acids with cyanide or sulfide compounds
- Oxidizers with organic solvents
- Water-reactive metals with water or aqueous solutions

When in doubt, the Lab Manager shall consult the SDS or contact the CHO before combining waste streams.

---

12. SAFETY DATA SHEETS (SDS)

12.1 **Availability**  
An SDS shall be readily accessible to all laboratory personnel for every chemical in the inventory. SDSs may be maintained in paper format in a binder, or in electronic format on a shared drive accessible from each laboratory workstation. The Lab Manager shall ensure that the SDS collection is complete and current.

12.2 **Acquisition**  
A current SDS shall be obtained from the supplier before a chemical is first used. If the supplier does not provide an SDS, the chemical shall not be accepted into the laboratory until the SDS is obtained. The SDS shall be filed in the laboratory SDS binder or uploaded to the shared drive within five working days of receipt of the chemical.

12.3 **Review and Update**  
SDSs shall be reviewed by the CHO at least annually. If a revised SDS is received from the supplier, the previous version shall be retained for reference for at least one year from the date of the revision, and the new version shall be clearly marked as the current version. The date of the most recent SDS revision shall be recorded in the chemical inventory.

documents.title: Laboratory Access Control Policy (Draft)
documents.content:
Access Level 3 (Independent Access): Entry into a laboratory outside normal working hours, or into a restricted research zone, for work that the user has been certified to perform independently. This level requires completion of all relevant safety modules and a written authorization from the Principal Investigator (PI) or Laboratory Supervisor.

Access Level 4 (Restricted Zone Access): Entry into designated high-risk zones, including but not limited to chemical storage rooms, autoclave rooms (when in use), and areas containing controlled biological agents. Access is granted on a case-by-case basis and requires additional clearance from the Laboratory Safety Officer (LSO) and, where applicable, the Institutional Biosafety Committee (IBC).

Access Level 5 (Emergency Access): Temporary access granted to emergency responders, maintenance personnel, or authorized individuals during an incident, spill, fire, or other urgent situation. Emergency access is not subject to the standard approval workflow but must be logged and reviewed retroactively.

---

ACCESS LEVELS AND ELIGIBILITY

The table below summarizes the minimum eligibility requirements for each access level.

| Access Level | Description | Minimum Training | Approval Authority | Validity |
|--------------|-------------|------------------|--------------------|----------|
| 1 | General Access (normal hours) | Lab Safety Induction (online) | PI or Lab Manager | Academic term or employment period |
| 2 | Supervised Access | Induction + Level 2 module (in-person) | PI or Lab Manager | Academic term or employment period |
| 3 | Independent Access | Induction + Level 2 + Level 3 modules (in-person, with assessment) | PI and LSO | 12 months, renewable |
| 4 | Restricted Zone Access | Level 3 + zone-specific training | LSO (and IBC for biological agents) | 6 months, renewable |
| 5 | Emergency Access | None required at time of entry | Incident Commander or Security | Single event, logged |

Note: Access Level 1 does not permit entry into laboratories that are designated as Level 3 or Level 4 zones, even during normal working hours.

---

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA

All applicants for access, regardless of level, must:
- Be affiliated with the University (or hold a valid visiting researcher status)
- Have a valid staff card, student card, or temporary access pass
- Have completed the online Lab Safety Induction within the past 12 months (for Levels 1–4)
- Not have any outstanding safety suspension or revocation on record

The Laboratory Access Control Policy draft header lists draft_version v0.4. Record status: historical.

Additional criteria for Level 3 and Level 4:
- The applicant must have completed at least one term of supervised laboratory work at the University, or provide documented equivalent experience from a recognized institution.
- The applicant must pass a practical assessment administered by the LSO or a designated trainer.
- The applicant must not have accumulated more than two safety violations in the preceding 12 months.

---

APPLICATION AND APPROVAL WORKFLOW

Step 1: Applicant submits a request through the Lab Access Portal (https://safety.nus.edu.sg/access), selecting the relevant access level and laboratory.

Step 2: The PI or Lab Manager reviews the request and confirms the applicant’s training status and eligibility. The PI may endorse or reject the request. Endorsement is given in writing via the portal.

Step 3: For Level 1 and Level 2, the PI’s endorsement is sufficient. The LSO is notified automatically and the access card is activated within 3 working days.

Step 4: For Level 3, the LSO reviews the application, verifies the practical assessment results, and approves or denies the request. The LSO may request additional documentation.

Step 5: For Level 4, the LSO reviews the application and, if the zone involves biological agents, forwards the request to the IBC for clearance. The IBC may impose additional conditions.

Step 6: The applicant is notified of the decision via email. Approved applicants receive a confirmation of access level and validity period.

Step 7: The access card is activated or updated by the Campus Security Office within 5 working days of approval.

3.3 Visiting Researchers

Visiting researchers are defined as individuals who are not employed by the University
and who are not enrolled as students, but who hold a valid visiting researcher status
issued by the University. Visiting researchers are subject to the general eligibility
criteria in Section 2 and to the following additional conditions:

- The visiting researcher must be sponsored by a PI who accepts responsibility for
  the visitor’s safety and conduct while on campus.
- The visiting researcher must complete the online Lab Safety Induction and any
  additional module required for the requested access level.
- The visiting researcher must not be granted access to Level 4 zones unless the
  visit is for a period exceeding 6 months and the IBC has given specific clearance.
- The visiting researcher’s access card is issued with a validity period not
  exceeding the duration of the visiting researcher status, and in any case not
  exceeding 6 months for Level 3 zones.

The LSO maintains a list of current visiting researchers and their access levels. The
list is reviewed at the start of each semester and whenever a visiting researcher
leaves the University.

---

SECTION 4: TRAINING REQUIREMENTS

4.1 General Training

All applicants must complete the online Lab Safety Induction before access is granted.
The induction covers general laboratory safety, emergency procedures, and the
University’s safety policies. The induction is valid for 12 months and must be
renewed annually.

4.2 Level-Specific Training

In addition to the general induction, the following training is required:

Level 1: No additional training.

Level 2: Chemical Safety Module (online, 2 hours) and, for access to Zone B,
equipment-specific training for each instrument.

Level 3: Practical assessment (as described in Section 2) and, for access to Zone C,
Chemical Storage Safety Module (in-person, 4 hours).

Level 4: Biosafety Module (in-person, 8 hours) and IBC protocol-specific training.
For access to Zone D, the applicant must be listed on the relevant IBC protocol.

documents.content:
SECTION 4: TRAINING REQUIREMENTS (continued)

4.3 Training Records

The LSO maintains training records for all access card holders. Each record contains the
applicant’s name, staff/student number, the modules completed with completion dates, and the
expiry date of each module. Records are updated within five working days of completion of a
module.

Training records are accessible to the following parties:

- The individual card holder, upon request.
- The PI or supervisor of the card holder, for the purpose of confirming that the
  individual remains eligible for the access level held.
- The LSO, for the purpose of audit and renewal processing.
- The University Safety Office, for the purpose of compliance audits.

Records are retained for a period of 3 years after the card holder’s access has lapsed or
been revoked, after which they are archived in accordance with the University Records
Management Policy.

4.4 Refresher and Update Requirements

The following refresher training is required to maintain an access level:

Level 1: No refresher training. The general induction must be renewed annually.

Level 2: The Chemical Safety Module must be renewed every 2 years. Equipment-specific
training is renewed only when the instrument or the operating procedure changes
significantly, as determined by the LSO in consultation with the PI.

Level 3: The practical assessment must be renewed every 3 years. The Chemical Storage
Safety Module must be renewed every 2 years.

Level 4: The Biosafety Module must be renewed annually. IBC protocol-specific training is
renewed whenever the protocol is amended or renewed, and in any case at least every 3
years.

The LSO sends a reminder to each card holder and to the relevant PI 30 days before any
training is due to expire. If the training expires, the access level is suspended
immediately and the card is deactivated until the training is completed and recorded.

4.5 Training Exemptions

Exemptions from any training module may be granted only by the LSO, in writing, on the
recommendation of the PI. An exemption is granted only when the PI certifies that the
applicant has demonstrated equivalent competency through prior training or experience, and
that the exemption does not compromise safety. Exemptions are recorded in the training
record with the basis for the exemption and the date of the recommendation. An exemption
does not extend the validity period of any other training module.

---

SECTION 5: ACCESS CARD ISSUANCE AND USE

5.1 Issuance

Access cards are issued by the LSO upon approval of an application and completion of all
required training. The card is issued with the access level and zone permissions approved
in the application. The card remains the property of the University and must be returned to
the LSO upon expiry, revocation, or cessation of the card holder’s affiliation with the
University.

5.2 Card Holder Responsibilities

The card holder must:

- Carry the access card at all times while in the laboratory complex.
- Not lend, transfer, or otherwise share the access card with any other person.
- Not allow any other person to enter a restricted zone using the card holder’s access.
- Report loss or theft of the access card to the LSO within 24 hours.
- Report any change in name, department, or PI to the LSO within 5 working days.

Failure to comply with these responsibilities may result in suspension of access and
disciplinary action under the University’s Staff and Student Conduct Policies.

5.3 Card Replacement

A replacement card is issued upon payment of the replacement fee as set out in the
University’s Schedule of Fees. The lost or stolen card is deactivated immediately upon
reporting. If a card is found after replacement, the card holder must return the original
card to the LSO.

5.4 Card Expiry and Renewal

Access cards expire on the date stated on the card. For staff, the expiry date is aligned
with the staff appointment end date. For students, the expiry date is aligned with the
expected graduation date. For visiting researchers, the expiry date is set in accordance
with Section 3.4.
